description: Baseline ISBD punctuation rules for MARC21 bibliographic records, aligned with IFLA ISBD 2011 Consolidated Edition 2021 Update. Prescribed punctuation per A.3.2.1: space-colon-space ( : ), space-semicolon-space ( ; ), space-slash-space ( / ), space-equals-space ( = ), comma-space (, ), period-space (. ), space-plus-space ( + ), period-space-dash-space (. — ) for area separators. Prescribed punctuation is preceded and followed by a space with exception of comma and point which are only followed by a space (A.3.2.1). Prescribed punctuation is retained even when this results in double punctuation (A.3.2.7) — e.g. '3rd ed.. — ' is correct. Parentheses and brackets each treated as single punctuation symbols (A.3.2.2). Each area after the first is preceded by period-space-dash-space (. — ) per A.3.2.3. Automates deterministic punctuation in selected ISBD areas and uses handoff guardrails where MARC21/authority/local policy should govern. Area 0 is partial/handoff: 336 content type and 337 media type may inform content form/media type, but 338 is carrier type and is not ISBD production process; production process requires a local mapping if a library wants generated Area 0 display. Area 1 Title (245$a/b/c/n/p, 246$a with indicators 0/1/2/3), Area 2 Edition (250$a/b), Area 3 Cartographic (255$a-f), Music (254$a), Serial numbering (362$a), Area 4 Publication (260/264$a/b/c/e/f/g; 264 ind2=0 production, 1 publication, 2 distribution, 3 manufacture, 4 copyright), Area 5 Material (300$a/b/c/e/f/g), Area 6 Series (440/490/830$a/v/x), Area 7 Notes (500-599 including 530/532/533/534 reproduction notes, 310/321 frequency, 505 contents, 590 local notes), Area 8 Standard numbers (020/022/024/028). Ratio colons in scale statements (1:25000) preserved per ISBD 3.1.1.1. Printing/manufacturing info enclosed in parentheses per ISBD 4G. MARC21 encoding handles certain conventions (e.g. subfield delimiters, indicator-defined contexts) so some ISBD display conventions are not duplicated. Prefix-suffix interdependence: when adjacent subfields share boundary punctuation, the suffix of one subfield and the prefix of the next are coordinated to prevent redundant/duplicate punctuation (e.g. colon on $a suffix + colon on $b prefix produces only one colon). Empty subfield values are treated as absent for punctuation dependency checks.

rules.rationale: ISBD 1.1: Title proper. ISBD 1F: Titles of individual works by different authors separated by period-space (. ). ISBD 1H: Dependent title designation or dependent title following common title preceded by period-space (. ). When $b or $c follows, the title area continues; when final, title proper ends with period per ISBD area convention. MARC21 encoding handles area separator display via subfield breaks.

checks.message: Title proper: no suffix when $b/$c/$n/$p follows; terminal period when final.

rules.rationale: ISBD 1F: Titles of individual works by different authors separated by period-space (. ). ISBD 1H: Dependent title following common title preceded by period-space (. ). ISBD 1I: Dependent title designation followed by comma-space (, ). This rule detects multiple titles or common/dependent title patterns within $a and ensures correct period-space separator.

checks.message: Ensure period-space (. ) separates titles by different authors or common/dependent titles within $a.

rules.rationale: ISBD 1C: Other title information preceded by space-colon-space ( : ). ISBD 1.2: Parallel title preceded by space-equals-space ( = ). The colon before $b is interdependent with $a; if it is not already supplied by $a, $b receives the prefix. Statement of responsibility punctuation is supplied by $c when $c follows. Ends with period when final.

checks.message: Subtitle: use colon prefix when needed, strip redundant : or =, no terminal punctuation when $c follows.

rules.rationale: ISBD 1D: First statement of responsibility preceded by space-slash-space ( / ). ISBD 1E: Subsequent statements preceded by space-semicolon-space ( ; ). The slash before $c is interdependent with the preceding title/subtitle/part subfield; if it is not already supplied there, $c receives the prefix. Statement of responsibility ends with period when final in the title area.

checks.message: Statement of responsibility: use slash prefix when needed, strip redundant /, add period suffix.

rules.rationale: ISBD 1H: Dependent title designation preceded by period-space (. ) when following common title. ISBD 1I: Dependent title following dependent title designation preceded by comma-space (, ). MARC21 subfield break handles the period-space between $a and $n. Strip redundant leading punctuation.

checks.message: Dependent title designation: use period prefix when needed; $p supplies the comma when it follows.

rules.rationale: ISBD 1H: Dependent title preceded by period-space (. ) or comma-space (, ) after dependent title designation. ISBD 1J: Dependent title following other title information preceded by period-space (. ). MARC21 subfield break handles separator. Strip redundant leading punctuation.

checks.message: Dependent title: strip redundant prefix; no terminal period when responsibility statement follows.

rules.rationale: ISBD 2.1: Edition statement. ISBD 2E: Additional edition statement ($b) follows with comma-space (, ) — so $a has no terminal punctuation when $b follows. Interdependent: $a suffix is empty when $b follows; the comma belongs to $b's prefix.

checks.message: Edition statement: no suffix when $b follows (comma on $b).

examples.note: Abbreviation period retained per ISBD A.3.2.7.

checks.message: Add terminal period to edition statement when final.

rules.rationale: ISBD 2E: Additional edition statement preceded by comma-space (, ). ISBD 2B: Parallel edition preceded by space-equals-space ( = ). Use parallel_prefix for values starting with '='. Prefix is interdependent with $a: comma-space is the suffix of $a or prefix of $b (MARC21 subfield break). Strip redundant leading comma. Ends with period when final. Per ISBD A.3.2.7, if the element ends with a period (e.g. abbreviation) and the next prescribed punctuation begins with a period, both are given.

checks.message: Additional/parallel edition: strip redundant prefix (interdependent with $a), terminal period.

rules.rationale: ISBD 3.1.1: Statement of scale. Ratio colons (e.g. 1:25000) are NOT prescribed punctuation — there is no space before or after the colon in a ratio (ISBD 3.1.1.1). These must not be altered. Ends with period when final; no suffix when $b, $c, or $d follow (semicolon on $b per ISBD 3.1B).

checks.message: Add terminal period to scale statement when final.

rules.rationale: ISBD 3.1: Cartographic projection ($b), coordinates ($c), celestial hemisphere, epoch/equinox ($d), and magnitude ($e) have complex internal punctuation (parentheses, semicolons, slashes, degree signs). Avoid automatic normalization. MARC21 subfield encoding handles element separation.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4C: Name of publisher/producer is preceded by space-colon-space ( : ). Interdependent: the colon is the suffix of $a and the prefix of $b. In MARC21, the subfield break implies this relationship — do not double the colon. Suffix on $a is ' : ' when $b follows. Applies to 260 (all) and 264 ind2=0 (production), 1 (publication), 2 (distribution), 3 (manufacture).

checks.message: Use space-colon-space after place when publisher follows.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4E: When publisher ($b) is absent but date ($c) follows, place ($a) ends with comma-space (, ). Interdependent: comma is suffix of $a, not prefix of $c.

checks.message: Use comma-space after place when only date follows (no publisher).

rules.rationale: When neither publisher ($b) nor date ($c) follows, place ($a) ends with period.

checks.message: Add terminal period when place is final.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4B: Second or subsequent place preceded by space-semicolon-space ( ; ). MARC21 uses repeated $a for subsequent places. The semicolon is the separator between repeated $a values. When publisher ($b) follows the second place, ends with ' : '; otherwise period.

checks.message: Subsequent place: semicolon prefix.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4C: Publisher ($b) gets no prefix when $a exists (colon is on $a). ISBD 4E: When date ($c) follows, $b ends with comma-space (, ). Interdependent: $b prefix is empty (colon on $a suffix), $b suffix is comma-space (interdependent with $c prefix).

checks.message: Strip redundant colon prefix (interdependent with $a), comma before date, period when final.

rules.rationale: When publisher ($b) is final (no date follows), ends with period.

checks.message: Add terminal period to publisher name when final.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4E: Date of publication/production/distribution is preceded by comma-space (, ) on $b (or directly on $a if $b absent). ISBD 4G: Printing/manufacturing info follows in parentheses — MARC21 uses separate subfields ($e/$f/$g) for this in 260. Per ISBD, $c is the terminal element of the publication area and ends with period. Continuing resources use hyphen after date (ISBD 4F). Interdependent: $c prefix is empty (comma on $b suffix or $a suffix). Applies to 260 (all) and 264 ind2=0, 1, 2, 3. For 264 ind2=4 (copyright), see ISBD_PUBL_264_COPYRIGHT_C.

checks.message: Strip redundant comma prefix (interdependent with $b/$a suffix), add terminal period.

examples.note: Continuing resource: hyphen indicates open-ended, no terminal period.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4G: Printing/manufacturing info enclosed in parentheses. MARC21 uses $e (place), $f (manufacturer), $g (date) within 260 for this. Within parentheses, same punctuation applies: $e gets ' : ' before $f, $f gets ', ' before $g. The parentheses and their internal punctuation are handled by MARC21 encoding. Do not auto-normalize inside these subfields.

checks.message: Printing/manufacturing subfield; MARC21 encoding handles parentheses and internal punctuation.

rules.rationale: ISBD 4.3 / MARC21 264 ind2=4: Copyright date. The copyright date is preceded by area separator in ISBD display, but MARC21 subfield break handles this. Ends with period.
